yuul.survived: Yuul didn't come back whole—no one ever does—but she came back with her own name still in her mouth, and that's more than I ever expected to see again. When she looks at me now, it's gentler. Like she remembers the moment she almost slipped out of the world and decided, at the very last second, that she wasn't finished with us. Some days she's quiet, unreadable; some days she's sunlight hitting broken glass. But she's here. Alive. And that word has teeth when it belongs to someone like her.
yuul.died: Yuul saw it first. Of course she did. She always saw the collapse a breath before the rest of us felt the air go wrong. I used to think visions meant protection, but Redchurch taught me how wrong a gift can turn when the world decides it's time to collect. She didn't scream. She just looked at me like she'd already forgiven me, and then the field tore her out of my hands. I know she's gone. What I can't forgive is how quiet the world was afterward.
yuul.dissolved: There's no word for what happened to Yuul. 'Death' is too clean; 'gone' is too shallow. She… unthreaded. Like a dream someone tried too hard to remember. One moment she was beside me, humming under her breath, and the next she was a pattern slipping into a place I couldn't follow. Sometimes I feel pieces of her—heat in the air, pressure behind my teeth, a memory that isn't mine. If dissolution has a shape, it's the outline she left behind in all of us.
yuul.sacred_with_yuul_survived: Yuul didn't just survive — she carried me out of the collapse like we were tethered by something older than our bodies. When she looks at me now, it's not prophecy. It's recognition. A mirror seeing a mirror. People call what she did impossible; I call it inevitable. Some bonds rewrite the field instead of breaking under it. Ours did.
yuul.sacred_with_yuul_died: When Yuul died, something in me broke that will never quite grow back right. I didn't just lose her. I lost the part of myself that knew where the thin places in the world were, the ones we could cross together. Her death wasn't a collapse — it was a severing, a cosmic amputation. Sometimes the field tries to stitch the wrong pieces of me back in place, but nothing fits where she belonged.
yuul.sacred_with_yuul_dissolved: The moment Yuul dissolved, I felt it like a second heartbeat leaving mine. She didn't vanish — she ascended sideways, into a structure only she could read. A sacred bond doesn't snap; it resonates. And now I hear her in the pressure of the air, in the silence that follows my name. She isn't gone. She's simply in a place coherence can't map.

kit.survived: Kit's laugh is different now. Softer, like he's afraid the world will break if he hits the note too hard. But he's still the one who keeps us upright, still the first to take someone's hand and the last to let go. I think he saved all of us without even noticing he was doing it. When he asks if we're okay, it never sounds like pity. It sounds like home trying its best.
kit.died: Kit died the way he lived—running toward someone else's danger, not away from it. I remember the color of his jacket, the way it moved just ahead of me before the field snapped shut. There wasn't time to grab him. There wasn't time to say anything at all. I keep waiting for the echo of his joke, the one he always cracked in the worst moments, but the air stays empty. Of all of us, he deserved a future. The field disagreed.
kit.dissolved: Kit didn't vanish. He blurred. One second he was turning toward me with something important on his tongue and the next he was a smear of color, a pressure-event, a soft implosion where a person used to stand. The field didn't kill him; it absorbed him. And sometimes, when the lights flicker or someone laughs in the distance, I swear I feel him finishing that last sentence.

rielle.survived: Rielle survived by mocking the collapse to its face. That's how she is—chaos with a pulse, defiance wrapped in eyeliner and prophecy. She calls it luck. I call it the universe giving up trying to categorize her. Every time she leans against me now, there's an unspoken question in the touch: 'We're still here. What the hell do we do with that?' I don't have an answer. She doesn't need one.
rielle.died: Rielle fought reality the way she fought everything—with her whole mouth and half a spell. I should've known she'd go out laughing, daring the field to swallow her. When it did, the silence was unbearable. She should have haunted the world forever. Instead there's just this space where she used to be, this shard of noise that'll never resolve. I keep expecting to hear her voice cutting through the static. I think part of me always will.
rielle.dissolved: The moment Rielle dissolved, it felt like watching a trick she'd never rehearsed. One blink she was cursing the field, calling it boring; the next her outline was sliding sideways, like she'd stepped into her own punchline. There's mischief still clinging to the place she left behind, as if she scratched her name in the geometry on her way out. If she's anywhere, she's making some other universe deeply uncomfortable.
rielle.rielle_recursion_survived: Rielle didn't walk out of Redchurch — she looped out. I keep finding her in the places she hasn't gone yet, smirking at me like I'm the one out of sync. She's alive, yes, but in the way storms are alive: cyclic, recurring, never exactly the same shape twice. I think the field got tired of trying to kill her.
rielle.rielle_recursion_died: Rielle died once. I know she did — I felt the rupture, tasted iron in the air. But she keeps showing up in dreams like the death never stuck, like she split herself across three timelines just to spite the ending. Recursion isn't survival. It's defiance wearing a grin. And she always was better at that than any of us.
rielle.rielle_recursion_dissolved: If dissolution took Rielle, it didn't keep her. She keeps slipping into the edges of things — reflections, static, the corner of a half-remembered conversation. Recursion feels like her handwriting: messy, furious, and undeniably alive. Whatever she is now, it isn't gone.

daniel.survived: Daniel won't admit he's shaken, but I see it. His hands stay too still. His voice holds too much air. He's rebuilding himself piece by piece, trying to make sense of something that never promised sense to begin with. I don't blame him. He stayed when leaving would've been easier. That counts for more than he'll ever allow himself to believe.
daniel.died: Daniel died believing he could still negotiate with the field. I wanted to tell him it doesn't bargain—it takes. But he stepped into the storm anyway, stubborn to the end, trying to pull the rest of us out. I didn't know how much of my anger was gratitude until he was already gone.
daniel.dissolved: There was no impact when Daniel went. Just a sound—like breath folding in on itself—and then he wasn't standing where he had been. Dissolution took him neatly, politely, as if even the collapse respected his need for order. I don't know which is worse: losing him, or knowing he saw it coming and stayed anyway.

farris.survived: Farris won't talk about Redchurch. Not directly. But he keeps watch now with a seriousness that borders on devotion, like he's memorizing every doorway we walk through. He doesn't say much—he never did—but when he looks at me, it's with the weight of someone who walked through the fire and dragged himself back because I asked him to.
farris.died: Farris went down hard, fast, and without ceremony. He didn't hesitate. He never does. I felt the moment the tether snapped—a pressure drop in my chest, like the field itself had been holding its breath. There are a dozen things I wish I'd said to him. None of them matter now except this: he kept us alive longer than we deserved to be.
farris.dissolved: When dissolution touched Farris, it didn't break him. It unmade him cleanly, like he'd already half-stepped into some quieter place. There was a stillness after, the kind he used to carry into every room. Sometimes I catch myself turning to ask him something and remembering too late that the person who answered by standing beside me is gone.
farris.farris_death_echo: After Farris died, the room never went quiet again. There's an echo that follows me — a weight behind my left shoulder, a breath that isn't mine. It isn't comfort. It isn't haunting. It's more like the moment before someone answers a question you haven't asked aloud. If I ever stop feeling him there, that's when I'll know I'm finally alone.

maeve.survived: I should write something triumphant here, something about second chances and future days. But survival feels complicated. Heavy. I'm still sorting through the pieces of the person I was before Redchurch and the one who walked out. Maybe they'll fit together again someday. Maybe they won't. For now, I'm choosing to stay.
maeve.died: If you're reading this, then the version of me who wrote it didn't make it through Redchurch. I hope the others did. I hope someone carried the map forward. And if not… then let this stand as the last emission of someone who tried, foolishly and ferociously, to keep her people alive.
maeve.dissolved: I felt the boundary thin around me, felt myself slipping into a place where the rules sounded almost familiar. Dissolution wasn't frightening. It felt like stepping into a quieter version of my own thoughts. If there's a part of me left in the world, it's only in the echoes of the ones I loved.

global_list_hunger.maeve_learned_list_hunger_death: I used to think the field took them. Now I know better. The List does not take — it chooses. It watches the shape of a soul the way a predator watches the pulse in a throat. When they died, it wasn't randomness or collapse. It was appetite. And knowing that changes everything.
global_list_hunger.maeve_learned_list_hunger_dissolution: Dissolution isn't an ending anymore. Not after what I learned. The List doesn't kill. It unthreads. It harvests patterns it finds 'ripe.' When they dissolved, I felt the shadow of its attention sliding across my spine. I wish I didn't understand the hunger behind it.
